Nicknamed ''Os Celestes'' (The Sky Blues), the club was founded in August 1923 as ''Club Celta'', following the merger of [[Real Vigo Sporting]] and [[Real Fortuna Football Club|Real Fortuna]]. The club's home stadium is [[Balaídos]], which seats 24,870 spectators. The club's name is derived from the [[Celts|Celtic peoples]] who once lived in Galicia. Celta have a long-standing rivalry with fellow Galician club [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo A Coruña]], with whom they contest the [[Galician derby]]. Celta have never won the league title nor [[Copa del Rey]], although they have reached the final three times in the latter. The club finished in their best-ever position of fourth in [[2002–03 La Liga|2002–03]], qualifying for the [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League]], where they were eliminated by [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in the round of 16. In the [[2016–17 UEFA Europa League]], Celta reached the semi-finals for the first time, losing to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. In [[2000 UEFA Intertoto Cup|2000]], Celta were one of the co-winners of the [[UEFA Intertoto Cup]]. ==History== ===Foundation=== [[File:Campo de Coia.jpg|thumb|265x265px|[[Campo de Coia]] (1908–1928)]] [[File:Copa Rey Alfonso XIII Celta de Vigo.png|thumb|275x275px|right|Copa del Rey Alfonso XIII' trophy in 1927]] [[File:BragavsCelta.jpg|thumb|265x265px|Real Club Celta de Vigo vs [[S.C. Braga]] in 1945]] RC Celta de Vigo was formed as a result of the ambition of Vigo's teams to achieve more at national level, where the [[Basque people|Basque]] sides had been their ''bête noire'' in the Spanish Championship. The idea was to merge both Vigo-based teams, [[Real Vigo Sporting]] and [[Real Club Fortuna de Vigo]], to create a more powerful team at national level. The standard-bearer of this movement was Manuel de Castro, known as "Handicap", a sports writer for the ''[[Faro de Vigo]]'' who, from 1915, began to write in his articles about the need for a unitarian movement.{{cite web |title="Todo por y para Vigo" |url=https://www.farodevigo.es/deportes/2013/08/23/vigo-17387098.html |website=Faro de Vigo |access-date=18 March 2023 |language=es |date=23 August 2013}} The slogan of his movement was ''"Todo por y para Vigo"'' ("All by and for Vigo"), which eventually found support among the managers of both clubs. It was backed unanimously when De Castro himself presented the motion at the assembly of the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] in [[Madrid]] on 22 June 1923. On 12 July 1923, the merger was approved at the annual general meetings of Vigo and Fortuna, held at the Cine Odeón and Hotel Moderno, respectively. At the last general meeting of Fortuna and Vigo, which approved the formation of the new club and was held on 10 August, the members decided on the name and colours of the team. Among the various names proposed were Club Galicia, Real Atlético FC, Real Club Olímpico, Breogán and Real Club Celta. The latter two names were the most liked and in the end they decided on Club Celta, an ethnic race linked to [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]]. The first president of Celta was Manuel Bárcena de Andrés, the Count of Torre Cedeira. This assembly also decided on the squad, which totaled 64 players and included some important players from Fortuna and Vigo, and was managed by [[Francis Cuggy]]. Their first match was a [[Exhibition game#Association football|friendly]] against Portuguese side [[Boavista F.C.|Boavista]], which Celta won 8–2. In January 1927, Celta won the 'Copa del Rey Alfonso XIII' trophy after defeating the English sailors team 4–1.{{cite web |title=El Mundo Deportivo, 24 January 1927 |url=http://hemeroteca-paginas.mundodeportivo.com/EMD02/HEM/1927/01/24/MD19270124-005.pdf |website=[[Mundo Deportivo]] |access-date=28 April 2024 |language=es}} In 1947–48, Celta ranked fourth, the club's joint highest ever finish, and reached the [[1948 Copa del Generalísimo final|Copa del Generalísimo final]], where they lost 4–1 to [[Sevilla FC]].{{cite web |title=Spain, Final Tables 1939–1949 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spanhist3949.html#4748 |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=18 March 2023}} Local striker [[Pahiño]], who took the [[Pichichi Trophy]] for 21 goals in 22 games that season, subsequently moved to [[Real Madrid]].{{cite news |title=Fallece Pahíño [''sic''], histórico goleador del fútbol español|trans-title= Pahiño, historic goalscorer of Spanish football, dies|url=https://www.marca.com/2012/06/12/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1339501563.html |access-date=9 March 2020 |work=Marca |date=12 June 2012 |language=es}} ===EuroCelta and subsequent decline=== [[File:Antes partido Celta Depor 2012.jpg|thumb|197x197px|Celta supporters before a match]] In the late 1990s and early 2000s, Celta were dubbed "EuroCelta" by the Spanish press as a result of their European performance. This included a 4–1 aggregate win against [[Liverpool FC|Liverpool]] in a run to the quarter-finals of the [[1998–99 UEFA Cup]].{{cite news |last1=Kelly |first1=Andy |title=Steven Gerrard Liverpool farewell: full Reds debut was only time 'I was pleased to be substituted' |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/steven-gerrard-liverpool-farewell-full-9193679 |access-date=9 March 2020 |work=Liverpool Echo |date=6 May 2015}} In the [[1999–2000 UEFA Cup|next season's edition]] they again reached the last eight, with a 4–0 second leg win over [[Juventus]] and a 7–0 home win against [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] (8–1 on aggregate).{{cite news |last1=Pereira |first1=Antonio Pedro |title=Celta 7–0 Benfica foi há 20 anos. Da volta triunfal à goleada sem volta|trans-title=Celta 7–0 Benfica was 20 years ago. From triumphant return to thrashing with no return |url=https://www.dn.pt/desportos/celta-7-0-benfica-foi-ha-20-anos-da-volta-triunfal-a-goleada-sem-volta-11548245.html |access-date=9 March 2020 |work=Diário de Notícias |date=25 November 2019 |language=pt}} Domestically, the team reached the [[2001 Copa del Rey final]], losing 3–1 to [[Real Zaragoza]] in [[Seville]].{{cite news |title=El Zaragoza vence al Celta y levanta su quinta Copa del Rey |trans-title=Zaragoza beat Celta and lift their fifth Copa del Rey|url=https://elpais.com/diario/2001/07/01/portada/993938401_850215.html |access-date=9 March 2020 |work=El País |date=1 July 2001 |language=es}} Key players during the period included [[Alexander Mostovoi]], [[Valery Karpin]] and [[Haim Revivo]], though the squad also relied upon other international players as well, such as goalkeeper [[Pablo Cavallero]]; defender and future coach [[Eduardo Berizzo]], midfielders [[Claude Makélélé]] and [[Mazinho]]; winger [[Gustavo Adrián López|Gustavo López]]; and strikers [[Catanha]] and [[Lyuboslav Penev]], amongst others. In 2002–03, under manager [[Miguel Ángel Lotina]], Celta ranked fourth, their highest finish since 1948, and qualified for the [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League]]. They reached the round of 16, where they were eliminated by [[Arsenal FC|Arsenal]] 5–2 on aggregate.{{cite news |title=Arsenal 2-0 Celta Vigo |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/champions_league/3543099.stm |access-date=9 March 2020 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=10 March 2004}} Domestically that year, the team came 19th and suffered relegation to the [[Segunda División]].{{cite news |title=Relegated Celta expect exodus |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/019d-0f84578009a4-7e845d7438a0-1000--relegated-celta-expect-exodus/ |access-date=9 March 2020 |publisher=UEFA |date=25 May 2004}} Although the squad was heavily dismantled following the demotion, Celta earned an immediate return to the top flight after finishing second in [[2004–05 Segunda División|2004–05]].{{cite news |title=Spanish duo celebrate promotion |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/025e-0f909d059d75-6ca1821adfff-1000--spanish-duo-celebrate-promotion/ |access-date=9 March 2020 |publisher=UEFA |date=18 June 2005}} In [[2006–07 La Liga|2006–07]], Celta finished 18th and were once again relegated to the Segunda División. The team subsequently fought against relegation to the third tier, and the risk of bankruptcy.{{cite news |title=El Celta pide que las instituciones le saquen de la quiebra económica|trans-title=Celta asks that the instuitutions save it from bankruptcy |url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/vigo/2007/11/09/celta-pide-instituciones-saquen-quiebra-economica/0003_6303302.htm |access-date=9 March 2020 |work=La Voz de Galicia |date=9 November 2007 |language=es}} This trend was bucked in the 2010–11 season, when new striker [[David Rodríguez Sánchez|David Rodríguez]], winger [[Enrique de Lucas]] and manager [[Paco Herrera]] helped them finish sixth. They were eliminated in the first knockout round by [[Granada CF|Granada]] after a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]], the game having finished 1–1 in 90 minutes.{{cite news |title=A trip down memory lane for Granada and Celta |url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/a-trip-down-memory-lane-for-granada-and-celta |access-date=9 March 2020 |publisher=La Liga |date=28 == ===Crest=== Celta's original crest was rather simple, featuring a red shield with two stylised letter Cs (Club Celta) and the [[Regalia of Spain|royal crown]] of Spain; in the year of its foundation, the club became one of a number of Spanish football clubs to be granted patronage by [[Alfonso XIII]] and thus the right to use the honorific ''real'' (Royal) in its name and the crown on its badge. The following year the shield's colour was changed to the traditional sky blue colour. Like many other Galician clubs, such as [[SD Compostela|Compostela]] and [[Racing de Ferrol|Racing Ferrol]], the crest also features the red [[cross of Saint James]] which was added in 1928.{{cite web|title=Historia del R.C. Celta de Vigo|url=http://www.fameceleste.com/p/historia-del-rc-celta-de-vigo.html|website=Fame Celeste}}{{cite web|title=Orígenes y escudo del Celta de Vigo|url=http://sextoanillo.com/index.php/2016/08/22/origenes-escudo-del-celta-vigo/|website=Sexto Anillo|date=22 August 2016 }}{{cite web|title=Celta de Vigo|url=http://herldicafutbolstica.blogspot.com/2009/02/celta-de-vigo.html|website=Heráldica Futbolística|date=17 February 2009 }} During the [[Spanish Second Republic]] (1931–1936), the honorific title and crown were removed from the club's name and crest; however, it was to return under the [[Spanish State]]. ===Kit=== Celta's home colours are sky blue and white. Originally, their home strip consisted of a red shirt, black shorts and blue socks. This was later changed at an unknown date to the current colours, representative of the [[Galician flag]]. {| |{{football kit | pattern_la = |pattern_b = _collar |pattern_ra = |pattern_sh = |pattern_so = _whitestripe | leftarm = E20E0E |body = E20E0E |rightarm = E20E0E |shorts = 000000 |socks = 0000FF |title=1923–1924}} |{{football kit | pattern_la = |pattern_b = |pattern_ra = |pattern_sh = |pattern_so = _band_white | leftarm = 87CEEB |body = 87CEEB |rightarm = 87CEEB |shorts = FFFFF |socks = 87CEEB |title=Current}} |} Celta had the longest-running sponsorship deal in Spanish football, and one of the longest-running in the world, with the French automobile manufacturer [[Citroën]] from 1985 to 2016.{{Cite web|date=2016-05-31|title=Citroën abandona la camiseta del Celta|trans-title=Citroën abandons Celta's shirt|url=https://www.farodevigo.es/deportes/2016/05/31/citroen-abandona-camiseta-celta-16602135.html|access-date=2021-02-11|website=Faro de Vigo|language=es}} The company established its plant within walking distance from Balaídos in 1958, and had first sponsored the club's women's basketball team in 1980.
